transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-12 15:30 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Tom (Redwood SE), Alina (CSM); Karen (CTO), Miguel (Head Infra), Priya (Security), Ethan (PM)

00:00 Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time today. Quick intro, I'm Samira, AE at Redwood, with Tom our SE.
00:08 Karen: Thanks Samira, hi all. We're doing a security posture review, want to understand where Redwood stands for handling PHI and our compliance bar.
00:14 Tom: Great, we'll run through SOC2/ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, encryption, and data retention. Happy to dive deeper - feel free to stop.
00:25 Miguel: Quick context, Pinnacle Health is evaluating hosted first but likely Dedicated or Private for production. We have EHR integrations and need to understand auditability and key management.
00:36 Priya: Specifically, we need to know if Redwood can meet SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, SAML SSO with our IdP, granular RBAC, and if audit logs include token-level data or request/response payloads.
00:48 Tom: Understood. At a high level: Redwood is SOC2 Type II certified and we also maintain ISO 27001 for our cloud control plane—I'll share the artifacts. For hosted, we offer encryption at rest and in transit, KMS integrations; for Dedicated and Private you can bring your own KMS in many cases.
01:05 Karen: When you say "share the artifacts", do you mean full reports or summarized evidence? Our security review team will want the actual SOC 2 report and scope.
01:12 Samira: We'll provide the SOC 2 Type II report and the ISO scope doc under an NDA if needed. I'll put that in the next steps.
01:20 Ethan: For SSO, we use Okta as our IdP and require SAML 2.0. We also want SCIM provisioning. Does Redwood support SAML + SCIM?
01:28 Tom: Yes, Redwood supports SAML 2.0 SSO for the control plane and SCIM provisioning for user lifecycle. In Dedicated/Private deployments, SSO is configurable with your IdP and you can enforce SAML-based SSO for the console and API keys issuance.
01:42 Priya: How is RBAC implemented? We need fine-grained roles—engineering can create hits, product can only view metrics, and security should have audit access.
01:50 Tom: Our RBAC supports roles and custom role mappings. You can map IdP groups to roles, and we expose least-privilege roles. There are some permissions that are only available to account admins in hosted offering but in Dedicated you get more control over admin roles.
02:05 Miguel: Audit logs: what exactly is logged? We need IP addresses, user identity, timestamp, and ideally request identifiers plus model version. Do you log payloads or redact them?
02:16 Tom: We log request metadata—user, timestamp, request id, model used, latency, tokens. For hosted, request/response payloads are not stored by default; we can enable additional logging under contract for troubleshooting but that has retention and privacy implications. For Dedicated/Private, logs can be kept in your VPC and forwarded to your SIEM—so you control retention and storage.
02:40 Priya: For PHI, we need to ensure encryption of data at rest with customer-managed keys. Is BYOK supported?
02:47 Tom: Yes, BYOK is supported for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we encrypt with managed keys but can offer customer-managed KMS for enterprise accounts—this is part of the security add-on.
02:58 Karen: Data residency: we need EU residency for some workloads and a US-only environment for others. Does Redwood allow region pinning?
03:05 Samira: Yes, you can pin workloads to regions. For Dedicated we provision clusters in the chosen region; for Private you can deploy into your VPC in the region you control. Hosted has region options but with multi-region fallback by default unless you explicitly request regional isolation.
03:22 Ethan: About retention: we need to keep logs for 7 years for certain audit reasons; can Redwood meet long-term retention for audit logs and model usage telemetry?
03:31 Tom: Retention is configurable. Hosted offers default retention windows (e.g., 90 days) but we have add-ons for extended retention and exports to S3/your logging pipeline for long-term storage. Dedicated/Private you control retention directly.
03:46 Miguel: What about encryption-in-transit—TLS? And mutual TLS for service-to-service?
03:50 Tom: TLS 1.2+ for all traffic; mTLS is supported for Dedicated/Private for service-to-service if you need stricter mutual auth.
04:00 Priya: The security team will ask about key rotation and HSM. Do you integrate with cloud HSMs or external HSM providers?
04:08 Tom: We integrate with AWS KMS / Cloud HSM and GCP KMS. For Private deployments you can plug in your on-prem HSM via our KMS integration layer. Key rotation policies are supported and we log key usage for audit.
04:22 Karen: On certifications: are there any gaps we should know about? We do a checklist.
04:27 Samira: The usual items—SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 cover many controls. For HIPAA/BAA, we do sign BAAs for enterprise customers—Tom can explain the deployment requirements for PHI.
04:38 Tom: To run under a BAA, we recommend Dedicated or Private; hosted can work but usually requires additional contractual controls and configuration—isolated tenants, litmus tests, and logs forwarded to your environment.
04:54 Miguel: Network controls—VPC peering, private endpoints, no public ingress?
04:58 Tom: Dedicated clusters can be provisioned with private endpoints and VPC peering. Private on-prem gives you full control. Hosted typically uses private links where available.
05:08 Ethan: Are there mechanisms for data deletion? For e-discovery and compliance we may need to purge data tied to a tenant or user.
05:15 Tom: Yes, we provide data deletion workflows and retention policies. For Hosted, deletion requests are processed through our control plane and we can provide attestations. For Dedicated/Private, you can run purge jobs in your environment.
05:30 Priya: Would you be able to run a small POC or benchmark? We want to simulate typical loads, and also validate latency and token-level cost.
05:38 Samira: Absolutely. Typical next step is an SE-led benchmark on Dedicated capacity. Tom, you'll own the test plan, right?
05:45 Tom: Yes, I'll draft a plan. We'll need a representative dataset and some sample prompts. We'll run throughput and tail latency tests and share the metrics.
05:55 Karen: On the legal side, we'll need the standard security questionnaire answered and the SOC 2 report before internal approval.
06:02 Samira: We'll fill out their questionnaire and send the SOC 2 under NDA.
06:08 Ethan: Pricing: can you share ballpark pricing for Dedicated vs Private for our scale—~50k tokens/day average, spikes to 250k?
06:18 Samira: I'll include pricing scenarios in the follow-up—Committed Dedicated vs pay-as-you-go Hosted. We typically show unit economics for token cost and expected latency.
06:26 Miguel: Any known limits to model variants or custom models in Dedicated? We have a custom fine-tuned model currently.
06:34 Tom: Dedicated supports customer models and fine-tuned variants; there are supported formats and a model onboarding process. For Private, you get full control. We may need to run compatibility checks for certain quantized formats.
06:47 Priya: Audit requirement: list of who accessed what and when. Is there an immutable audit trail?
06:53 Tom: We write append-only audit events. For Hosted we retain them for the configured window; for Dedicated/Private you can ship them to your SIEM for immutable storage and longer retention.
07:05 Karen: Are penetration test results available?
07:09 Samira: We have summarized pentest reports and can share redacted results. We also run regular vulnerability scans and maintain a CVE remediation process.
07:20 Miguel: Does Redwood support data classification tags so we can mark PHI and apply different retention rules?
07:26 Tom: We have tagging and metadata on requests in Dedicated/Private that can be used to drive retention and routing policies—e.g., route PHI to Private. Hosted supports request tagging but enforcement may require contract-level controls.
07:40 Ethan: Any third-party subprocessors? We need a list for vendor management.
07:45 Samira: We'll send a current list of subprocessors and their roles; it's part of the security package.
07:53 Priya: How about disaster recovery, RTO/RPO SLAs, and backup encryption?
07:58 Tom: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and documented RTO/RPO targets; backups are encrypted and for Private you control backup storage.
08:08 Karen: Ok let's recap so we can move internal review.
08:12 Samira: Recap: Redwood will send SOC2 Type II and ISO scope, SCIM/SAML integration docs, sample RBAC mappings, audit log schema, BYOK/KMS details, and subprocessors list. Redwood SE will run a Dedicated benchmark once Pinnacle shares test dataset. Pricing scenarios for Hosted/Dedicated/Private will be provided.
08:28 Miguel: Sounds good. We'll send our security questionnaire and provide a contact for the legal team.
08:33 Samira: Great. We'll aim to get the artifacts over within three business days. Tom will follow up on the benchmark plan.
08:41 Tom: I'll schedule the technical deep dive—looking at availability next week.
08:45 Karen: Thanks everyone.

(occasional cross talk and short pauses omitted)
